_comment: Function families for auditing Lectern's filter by TITLE rather than by posting. Professor Bear's design, 2026-09-26: there are far fewer job FUNCTIONS than job postings, so classifying titles into families turns a 3,446-row read into a 15-row judgment. Order matters — first match wins — so the most specific families come first. Every family is a hypothesis about what a word means in this industry, and the report shows where the hypothesis was wrong.

families.name: ML_TRAINING
families.note: FALSE FRIEND, and the reason this family is first. At an AI company 'training' overwhelmingly means training a MODEL, not teaching a person. 25 of the 27 postings whose titles contain a teaching word were actually these. Any audit that treats 'training' as education will report the filter as broken when it is right.

families.name: TEACHING
families.note: People being taught. This is the target.

families.name: ADVOCACY
families.note: Teaching a public rather than a classroom. Also the target.

families.name: MATERIALS
families.note: ADDED 2026-09-26. Jobs whose product is the MATERIALS — docs, guides, tutorials, courseware, reference builds. Anthropic's 'Technical Documentation and Content Engineer, Claude Docs' is the model. Note how thin this is by title: 'documentation' appears in 2 of 3,446 titles and 'technical writer', 'curriculum', and 'instructional design' in ZERO. This family is nearly invisible to a title search, which is itself the finding.

families.name: SALES_ENABLEMENT
families.note: REVERSED 2026-09-26 by Professor Bear: "developing materials… to train their own people would be a great fit." Sales enablement builds curriculum, runs live training, and produces onboarding content for the company's own staff — that is the work, and the audience being internal does not change it. These 13 postings were classed as false positives by the previous version of this file; they are not.

families.name: TECH_ENABLEMENT
families.note: FALSE FRIEND. Here 'enablement' means making a system capable of something. These are engineering jobs. Still a reject: here 'enablement' describes a system gaining a capability, with no materials and no audience.

families.name: CUSTOMER_ENABLEMENT
families.note: GENUINELY AMBIGUOUS. Customer enablement does teach — live training, workshops, adoption plans — but for paying accounts, with renewal risk attached. Whether it counts is a judgment about what the searcher wants, not a fact about the posting.

families.name: EDU_SALES
families.pattern: \b(higher education|k.?12|education|academic|university|campus|student) (account (executive|manager)|sales|business development|partnerships? (manager|lead)|growth|recruiter)\b|\b(account executive|business development representative|account manager),? \(?(higher education|k.?12|education)
families.note: MOVED to judge 2026-09-26: Professor Bear's target includes developing materials "to sell into universities." A Higher Education Account Executive who only carries a quota is still a reject; one who builds the curriculum and enablement materials the sale runs on is a fit. The title alone cannot tell them apart, so each is a judgment.

families.name: RECRUITING
families.note: FALSE FRIEND, and the one that caught the topic-word rule out. 'University', 'campus', and 'student' are campus-recruiting vocabulary as much as teaching vocabulary.

families.name: COMMUNITY
families.note: AMBIGUOUS. A developer-community manager teaches; a data-centre community-engagement manager does local-government relations; a security-community lead runs vulnerability disclosure. Same word, three jobs.
